record.paper_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
record.context_brief: Policy constraints under multimodal behavior data
record.original_question: How can offline reinforcement learning impose policy constraints against the behavior represented in a dataset when that behavior is highly multimodal, without relying on an estimated behavior-policy model that averages across modes and thereby permits out-of-distribution actions?

evidence.quote: This means that the performance of these algorithms is limited by the accuracy of estimation of the behavior policy, which may be hard in scenarios with highly multimodal behaviors, as is the case in practice with real-world problems. For example, if a unimodal Gaussian policy is used to model a highly multi-modal action distribution, averaging across different modes while fitting this behavior policy may actually be unable to prevent the learned policy, π, from choosing out-of-distribution actions. Methods that enforce the constraint implicitly, using only samples and without explicit behavior policy estimation, are a promising way to alleviate this limitation (Peng et al., 2019; Nair et al., 2020).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an offline reinforcement learning setting in which a learner is given a fixed dataset D = {(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)} of transitions generated by an unknown behavior policy π_β(a | s) on a Markov decision process (S, A, P, r, γ). The goal is to learn a policy π(a | s) that maximizes the expected discounted return while remaining "close" to the behavior data, so as to avoid evaluating the learned Q-function at out-of-distribution actions.

A common strategy is to enforce an explicit policy constraint of the form D(π(· | s) ‖ π̂_β(· | s)) ≤ ε, where π̂_β is a parametric estimate of π_β fit to D (e.g., a unimodal Gaussian) and D is a probability divergence. When the true behavior policy π_β(· | s) is highly multimodal, fitting a unimodal (or otherwise mode-averaging) parametric model π̂_β can produce a density whose support includes regions between the modes that contain no data; constraining π to stay close to such an estimate therefore fails to keep π within the support of the data and permits the selection of out-of-distribution actions.

Problem. Design and analyze an offline reinforcement learning algorithm that constrains the learned policy π to the (possibly highly multimodal) distribution of actions actually present in D, using only samples from D and without fitting an explicit generative model π̂_β of the behavior policy. Specifically, propose a constraint mechanism (e.g., implicit, sample-based, or value-based) such that:

(a) for every state s in the support of D, π(a | s) places negligible probability mass on actions a that lie outside the support of π_β(· | s), even when π_β(· | s) has multiple well-separated modes;
(b) the procedure does not require evaluating, sampling from, or differentiating through any learned density model of π_β; and
(c) the resulting algorithm admits a guarantee (theoretical or quantifiable empirical bound) on the suboptimality of π relative to the best policy supported on the data.

Formulate such a constraint, prove that it avoids the mode-averaging failure mode described above, and characterize conditions under which the resulting policy improvement step is safe with respect to out-of-distribution action selection.
artifact.status_search_result: Several lines of subsequent work have proposed implicit, sample-based, or support-based constraint mechanisms that avoid fitting an explicit unimodal behavior model — for example, advantage-weighted regression style methods (AWR/AWAC), energy-based implicit constraints, Morse-network implicit behavior models, supported policy optimization (SPOT), and Q-function-based steering toward the behavior policy. These provide partial answers, especially empirically, but a fully general algorithm with rigorous guarantees on safety against out-of-distribution actions under arbitrarily multimodal behavior remains an active research area; no single method is recognized as a definitive solution.

status_evidence.title: Supported Policy Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Steers a learning policy toward the behavior policy support without explicit density estimation.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a sample-based support-constraint approach addressing multimodal behavior.

status_evidence.title: Implicit policy constraint for offline reinforcement learning
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses distribution shift via implicit constraints with energy-based models rather than explicitly modelling the behaviour policy, avoiding multi-modal behaviour policy representation issues.
status_evidence.claim: Implicit (energy-based) constraints partially address the multimodal behavior issue.

status_evidence.title: RAMAC: Multimodal Risk-Aware Offline Reinforcement Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continuing to study behavior regularization under multimodal behavior data.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: BDQL: Offline RL via Behavior Diffusion Q-learning without Policy Constraint
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes diffusion-based methods to handle multimodal behavior without an explicit policy constraint.
status_evidence.claim: Diffusion/implicit modeling is one of several proposed partial solutions.
